stage: Q5-2 graded termination buffer radial size matching, self-gated

rule.statement: No graded termination buffer row may be radially thicker than the remainder background cell it borders. The buffer is a locally reduced march, so it is re-resolved with more, thinner rows at the same total thickness rather than cut afterwards.
rule.growth_ratio: largest ratio in (1, original] whose outermost row is <= cap; at fixed total thickness a larger ratio keeps the first row thinner, preserving near-wall grading
rule.cap: outerTransitionRadialTargetCells * remainderCellSize, reusing the Q5-1 value of 1.0

why_self_gated.difference_from_q5_1: The fan is explicitly interpolated ring by ring, so Q5-1 could write the last row offset as ring + rows/rows and keep the outer envelope bit-identical. The buffer front is stepped and produced by buildLocallyReducedBoundaryLayerStrips2D, where each column's layer count comes from a local collision/concavity test.
why_self_gated.consequence: Holding the requested total thickness does not hold the actual stepped front: a column that could only march 2 of 3 rows to 0.0447 may march 3 of 6 thinner rows to 0.0554. The remainder therefore changes.
why_self_gated.post_hoc_subdivision_rejected: At a step the outermost cell's radial face is itself on the outer envelope, so radial subdivision inserts collinear vertices into the remainder boundary loop. strictlyConvex treats cross <= 1e-10*scale as concave, so every such Cut cell would be force-ear-clipped, which is the sliver mechanism measured during the Q5-1 closeout. canonicalizeTransitionEnvelope2D early-returns under localTermination, so nothing removes those vertices.
why_self_gated.gate: Build both fronts, commit the re-resolved one only on a strict typed hard-count decrease. A tie keeps the historical march.

diagnosis.method: every hard face split by the cell kinds on both sides; Termination cells further separated into buffer rows 1/2/3 versus remainder-derived by graph distance from the H4-1 layer

concave_l.outcome: declined; hybrid.cm2d, hybrid.solver.cm2d and hybrid.quality-contract.json byte-identical to baseline

narrow_gap.note: without the gate this geometry would have gained 74 percent more hard issues, which is why the rule is not applied unconditionally

circle_and_superellipse.outcome: localReductionApplied is false, so Q5-2 is inert; solver .cm2d byte-identical to the Q5-1-only build (circle WARN with 0 hard, superellipse 12 hard)

q52_sharp_trailing_edge.note: max aspect ratio improves from 13.912 on the Q4-1 sharp-tail mesh

cost: With the flag on, every localTermination geometry builds two fronts, i.e. two full hybrid builds. This is a global candidate comparison rather than a patch-local selection. Zero cost with the flag off.

regression_gates_added.unit_test: tests/h4_local_termination_test.cpp asserts the sharp taper stays Hybrid under a Q5-2 policy, that committed equals matched < historical, and that this geometry is a measured win
regression_gates_added.ci: cartmesh2d-ci.yml builds q52_concave_l, q52_sharp_trailing_edge and q52_narrow_gap; asserts committed == (matched < historical), historical == baseline, after <= before, byte identity with the baseline when declined, a strict decrease on the sharp taper, plus independent reader and checkMesh coverage

remaining.term_buf1_versus_boundary_layer: concave_l 44, sharp_trailing_edge 38, narrow_gap 34 hard faces where the buffer's FIRST row is larger than the H4-1 layer cell under it. Opposite direction to this rule; raising the growth ratio already thins that row but no criterion targets it.
remaining.declined_geometries: concave_l and narrow_gap keep their Term(rem) <- Term(buf3) family (176 faces on narrow_gap). Reaching it needs a buffer subdivision that preserves the stepped front, which first requires resolving collinear vertices being classified concave by strictlyConvex, the route the Q2 document records as blocked.
